boundaryNote: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods are matched by official codes to its October 2026 profiles of the 2021 Census. Every profile identifies neighbourhood definitions from June 2020. The 2026 boundary-bylaw amendment changes three names. Its annex swaps two description headings; Article 1 and the profile maps confirm 5-1 as Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux and 5-4 as Vieux-Bourg. Display polygons come from the 2026-11-01 municipal extract; exact historical vertex identity is not asserted. Coverage is the City of Québec. The neighbouring municipalities of L'Ancienne-Lorette and Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, and the Wendake reserve, are outside these polygons; wider agglomeration and metropolitan observations are not used.
coverageNote: Population and housing describe 2021. Apartments under five storeys are a specific dwelling category, not all apartments. Park figures cover school, dog and linear park locations only; ordinary neighbourhood parks are not covered. Library sites include institutional libraries. Current facility and RTC stop inventories have their own dates. Parkland area, rail, tram, commuting shares, occupations and current rents are not collected in this bundle.

population.label: Residents
population.note: Published 2021 resident population, including people outside private households. Read from the neighbourhood's own highlights, printed page 5 of its October 2026 profile; source rounding is retained.
population.geographicScope: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods defined in June 2020; no CMA or agglomeration observations.

households.label: Private households
households.note: Published 2021 private-household count in the profile's population and household highlights. Rounded independently of the housing table. Read from the neighbourhood's own highlights, printed page 5 of its October 2026 profile; source rounding is retained.
households.geographicScope: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods defined in June 2020; no CMA or agglomeration observations.

householdSize.label: Average household size
householdSize.note: Published average persons per private household; not total population divided by households. Read from the neighbourhood's own highlights, printed page 5 of its October 2026 profile; source rounding is retained.
householdSize.geographicScope: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods defined in June 2020; no CMA or agglomeration observations.

livingAlone.label: One-person households
livingAlone.note: Published share of private households with one person; not the share of residents living alone. Read from the neighbourhood's own highlights, printed page 5 of its October 2026 profile; source rounding is retained.
livingAlone.geographicScope: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods defined in June 2020; no CMA or agglomeration observations.

occupiedDwellings.label: Occupied private dwellings
occupiedDwellings.note: Published housing-table count of occupied private dwellings. The rounded count can differ from the private-household count. Read from the neighbourhood's own highlights, printed page 5 of its October 2026 profile; source rounding is retained.
occupiedDwellings.geographicScope: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods defined in June 2020; no CMA or agglomeration observations.

detached.label: Detached homes
detached.note: Published share of occupied private dwellings that are single-detached houses (maisons individuelles). Read from the neighbourhood's own highlights, printed page 5 of its October 2026 profile; source rounding is retained.
detached.geographicScope: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods defined in June 2020; no CMA or agglomeration observations.

lowRiseApartments.label: Apartments under five storeys
lowRiseApartments.note: Published share of occupied private dwellings in apartment buildings with fewer than five storeys. Excludes taller apartment buildings and duplexes; it is not the total apartment share. Read from the neighbourhood's own highlights, printed page 5 of its October 2026 profile; source rounding is retained.
lowRiseApartments.geographicScope: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods defined in June 2020; no CMA or agglomeration observations.

renters.label: Renter households
renters.note: Published share of private households that rent their dwelling. Census tenure is not current rental availability. Read from the neighbourhood's own highlights, printed page 5 of its October 2026 profile; source rounding is retained.
renters.geographicScope: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods defined in June 2020; no CMA or agglomeration observations.

majorRepairs.label: Homes needing major repairs
majorRepairs.note: Published share of occupied private dwellings reported as needing major repairs at the 2021 census; not a current inspection. Read from the neighbourhood's own highlights, printed page 5 of its October 2026 profile; source rounding is retained.
majorRepairs.geographicScope: The City's 35 administrative neighbourhoods defined in June 2020; no CMA or agglomeration observations.

parks.label: School, dog and linear park sites
parks.note: Distinct names from Lieux publics points classified Parcs écoles, Parc canin or Parcs linéaires. The dataset contains only these limited park categories; ordinary neighbourhood parks are not covered. Multiple points for the same name inside one neighbourhood count once. These are mapped locations, not park footprints, all parks, parkland area or walking access. A zero means no selected site, not no parks.
parks.geographicScope: Point-in-polygon assignment to original 2026-11-01 neighbourhood polygons in NAD83 / MTM zone 7 (EPSG:32187). Shared-edge ties go to the lowest neighbourhood code; outside points are excluded.

busStops.label: RTC bus-stop locations
busStops.note: Distinct GTFS stop IDs inside each neighbourhood in the RTC feed valid for these dates. Opposite-direction stops count separately. The feed inventory does not measure frequency or confirm that every listed stop is served on a particular day; rail and a proposed tramway are not counted.
busStops.geographicScope: Point-in-polygon assignment to original 2026-11-01 neighbourhood polygons in NAD83 / MTM zone 7 (EPSG:32187). Shared-edge ties go to the lowest neighbourhood code; outside points are excluded.

libraries.label: Mapped library sites
libraries.note: Lieux publics sites classified Bibliothèques; same-name records less than 100 metres apart are merged. The inventory includes institutional libraries, including Université Laval and Collège des Jésuites; counts do not imply unrestricted public access or opening hours.
libraries.geographicScope: Point-in-polygon assignment to original 2026-11-01 neighbourhood polygons in NAD83 / MTM zone 7 (EPSG:32187). Shared-edge ties go to the lowest neighbourhood code; outside points are excluded.

communityCentres.label: Mapped community centres
communityCentres.note: Distinct Lieux publics points classified Centres communautaires. Other source classes, including Centres de loisirs, Centres récréatifs and Patros, are excluded. Counts do not measure capacity or opening hours.
communityCentres.geographicScope: Point-in-polygon assignment to original 2026-11-01 neighbourhood polygons in NAD83 / MTM zone 7 (EPSG:32187). Shared-edge ties go to the lowest neighbourhood code; outside points are excluded.

sources.title: Quartiers — official neighbourhood boundaries
sources.licence: Attribution (CC-BY 4.0)
transformations: Explicit 35-ID/profile-code crosswalk checked against publisher names.
Original polygons used for spatial joins in EPSG:32187; display simplified by 8 metres and oriented clockwise.
notes: All October 2026 profiles explicitly say their neighbourhood is defined since June 2020. R.V.Q.2301 took effect on 2 June 2020. The current D-8 bylaw records R.V.Q.3519, effective 22 April 2026, as a naming amendment: Orsainville, Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux and Vieux-Bourg.
The current map extract is not represented as an archived 2021 vertex dataset. The administrative-definition evidence supports the join; source geometry can receive cartographic corrections.

sources.title: Portraits sociodémographiques des 35 quartiers — October 2026 editions
sources.licence: Statistics Canada Open Licence for census observations; municipal profile documents retain publisher rights.
transformations: pdftotext extracts physical pages 1–7; parse only the neighbourhood's own FAITS SAILLANTS statements on printed page 5.
French decimal commas and thousands spaces normalized; rounded published percentages are retained without recomputing denominators.
notes: Each row identifies its individual PDF source. All 35 profiles explicitly describe June 2020 neighbourhood definitions.
Later comparative chart sections are not used: some PDFs contain unrelated neighbourhood headers and some charts are embedded images.
Missing/suppressed values remain null. A changed label, geography assertion or profile identity stops the build. No current rent, all-apartment share or CMA figure is inferred.

sources.title: R.R.V.Q. D-8 neighbourhood boundaries and amendments R.V.Q.2301 / R.V.Q.3519
sources.licence: Official municipal legal documents; no separate reuse licence stated.
notes: 2020 amendment: https://reglements.ville.quebec.qc.ca/fr/document/an/R.V.Q.2301/
2026 amendment: https://reglements.ville.quebec.qc.ca/fr/document/an/R.V.Q.3519/
2020 annex: https://reglements.ville.quebec.qc.ca/fr/ressource/ra/R.V.Q.2301_FR_001_0001.pdf
2026 annex: https://reglements.ville.quebec.qc.ca/fr/ressource/ra/R.V.Q.3519_FR_001_0001.pdf

The April 2026 explanatory note states that three neighbourhood designations change. Independent comparison found all 35 boundary-description bodies unchanged after whitespace normalization between the 2020 and 2026 annexes; this is textual-boundary evidence, not historical GIS vertex identity.

Publisher anomaly: the 2026 annex transposes the Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux and Vieux-Bourg description headings. Article 1 correctly assigns 5-1 to Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux and 5-4 to Vieux-Bourg. Both October 2026 profile maps and current municipal GIS support that mapping; the erroneous annex headings are not used for the join.

sources.title: Lieux publics — school, dog and linear park sites only
sources.licence: Attribution (CC-BY 4.0)
transformations: Select only exact DESCRIPTION classes Parcs écoles, Parc canin and Parcs linéaires.
Count distinct park names per neighbourhood after original-point assignment.
notes: 89 selected park point records; 0 outside neighbourhood polygons excluded.
The snapshot has 85 school-park, 2 dog-park and 2 linear-park point records. Repeated names within a neighbourhood count once; the locations do not represent park footprints.

Ordinary neighbourhood parks and parkland area are not covered by these source categories. The separate municipal ArcGIS recreation-map inventory was not imported because its metadata did not state a reuse licence.

sources.title: Lieux publics — library and community-centre points
sources.licence: Attribution (CC-BY 4.0)
transformations: Select exact DESCRIPTION classes Bibliothèques and Centres communautaires; assign original points to neighbourhood polygons.
Library names are normalized by removing the Bibliothèque prefix; same-name locations less than 100 metres apart are merged, retaining the lowest source ID.
notes: The municipal inventory includes municipal facilities and some private institutions. Library sites are not restricted to public-library network branches.
The snapshot has two nearby records for Maison de la Littérature: IDs 102399 and 202454, on adjacent streets. They count as one site (ID 102399). This reduces 28 library records to 27 sites.
Outside polygons excluded: 0 library and 0 community-centre points.

notes: 4318 stops in the regional feed; 276 points outside Québec City neighbourhood polygons excluded.
Inventory only: no calculation of active service, route frequency, walking distances or day-specific accessibility. Rail and proposed tram infrastructure are not included.
